title: Release plan: staged enablement + feature flags + backout playbook for SLO-based auto-rollback
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Context
We’re shipping the auto-rollback-on-SLO-breach capability for model rollouts (canary + A/B). This ticket defines how we roll out the feature itself safely (env-by-env / route-by-route), what feature flags gate behavior, required pre-reqs (monitors + dashboards + runbooks), and how to back out quickly if we see false positives, oscillation, or controller instability.

Primary goals
- Prevent unintended rollback/pause actions in production while we validate semantics and monitor coverage.
- Ensure we can disable the feature in <5 minutes without redeploying.
- Ensure we don’t introduce alert/paging storms.

Non-goals
- No changes to SLO semantics / breach evaluation logic beyond what’s already implemented under ENG-4861 + ADR-0127.

Feature flags / config gates
1) rollout.auto_actions.enabled (global)
- Default: false in all envs.
- When false: controller still evaluates (optional) but MUST NOT execute pause/rollback; emits eval metrics only (if eval flag enabled).

2) rollout.auto_actions.mode (enum)
- Values: OFF | EVAL_ONLY | PAUSE_ONLY | ROLLBACK_ALLOWED
- Default: OFF
- Notes:
  - EVAL_ONLY: record evaluation outcome + suppression reasons, but no state changes.
  - PAUSE_ONLY: can pause rollout steps, but cannot rollback traffic split.
  - ROLLBACK_ALLOWED: can execute rollback executor (traffic shift + revert to last known good).

3) rollout.auto_actions.scopes.allowlist (scoped enablement)
- Format: allowlist by (service/route, model_family, region, customer_tier)
- Required for any non-OFF mode in staging/prod.
- Rationale: we want to start with 1 internal route + 1 region + self-serve tier.

4) rollout.auto_actions.suppress_during_incident (global)
- Default: true in prod.
- Uses existing “incident mode”/known outage toggle (see SRE thread 1770246692). If incident mode is active, action execution is suppressed; still log suppression reason.

5) rollout.auto_actions.notification.enabled
- Default: true once we go beyond EVAL_ONLY in staging; in prod, true but routed as notify-only initially (no paging).

Pre-flight requirements (hard gates before enabling per scope)
- Monitors present and marked safe for auto-actions (SLO coverage audit: Drive sheet + monitor adapter freshness checks)
  - Latency p95/p99 SLO for target route scope
  - Error rate SLO (5xx / request failures)
  - Staleness detection configured (monitor timestamp + sample size)
- Dashboards + alert rules merged and deployed (observability-pack PR-913)
- Runbook published and reviewed with oncall (ENG-4855)
- Incident-bot message formatting validated in staging (ENG-4872)
- E2E tests passing in staging with synthetic signal injection (ENG-4844)

Staged enablement plan
Phase 0: Dev (internal)
- Target: dev control-plane + console dev
- Mode: EVAL_ONLY for all scopes
- Checklist:
  - Validate metric labels/cardinality for rollout_id, service, route, region, tier
  - Validate audit events emitted for: EVAL_OK / EVAL_BREACH / SUPPRESSED / MONITOR_STALE
  - Confirm controller behavior on missing data: do not act; record suppression reason

Phase 1: Staging (limited)
- Target scope allowlist:
  - Service: inference-gateway
  - Route: /v1/chat/completions (staging)
  - Region: us-east-1
  - Tier: internal/self-serve only
- Week 1: EVAL_ONLY
  - Run synthetic latency spike + 5xx spike to confirm evaluator transitions and debounce behavior
  - Validate Slack notifications are “notify-only” and include dashboard links + rollout id
- Week 2: PAUSE_ONLY
  - Expected outcome: controller pauses rollout step when fast burn triggers and min-sample is satisfied
  - Confirm pause is idempotent and doesn’t wedge rollout state machine
- Week 3: ROLLBACK_ALLOWED
  - Only after 2+ game-day runs with no false positives and no step transition races (see PR-28502)
  - Confirm rollback executor step-down (rate-limited traffic shift), and idempotency (repeated executions safe)

Phase 2: Prod (internal canary)
- Target scope allowlist:
  - 1 internal production route with low customer blast radius (to be nominated by Platform; currently proposal: internal-evals route)
  - Single region (us-east-1)
  - Tier: internal only
- Mode progression:
  - Start EVAL_ONLY for 48 hours (baseline noise check)
  - Move to PAUSE_ONLY for 72 hours
  - Move to ROLLBACK_ALLOWED only after SRE sign-off email (20260212 thread)
- Alerting:
  - Notify to #eng-sre and #eng-platform; no paging until we see stable behavior

Phase 3: Prod (expanded)
- Expand allowlist:
  - Add 1 customer-facing self-serve route in one region
  - After 1–2 weeks: add remaining regions for self-serve tier
  - After stability: enable for Dedicated tier (per-customer opt-in) and Private (case-by-case)
- Controls:
  - Tier gating remains mandatory; do not enable Dedicated/Private by default
  - Require per-service owner acknowledgement in ticket/comment before adding to allowlist

Backout / rollback plan (feature-level)
Immediate disable (no deploy)
- Set rollout.auto_actions.mode = OFF globally
- Ensure rollout.auto_actions.enabled = false
- Keep EVAL_ONLY available for debugging only (optional)

Partial backout options
- Downgrade from ROLLBACK_ALLOWED -> PAUSE_ONLY if rollback executor is problematic but evaluation seems correct.
- Disable Slack notifications if noise is too high (keep audit events + metrics).
- Remove a problematic scope from allowlist (service/route/region/tier) while leaving others enabled.

Backout criteria (automatic “stop the line”)
- Any unintended rollback (false positive) in prod impacting external traffic
- Rollout controller instability:
  - crash loops, elevated reconcile latency, stuck rollouts > 10 minutes attributable to auto-actions
- Monitor/data issues:
  - widespread stale monitor alerts leading to high suppression counts (>20% of evaluations) for enabled scopes
- Paging storm risk:
  - >5 auto-action notifications per 10 minutes across enabled scopes (tune thresholds/notification routing)

Comms plan
- Phase changes announced in #eng-platform and #eng-sre (include scope allowlist and mode)
- For first prod canary: send email to oncall alias with runbook link + explicit backout steps
- If we hit backout criteria: incident commander empowered to set OFF immediately; follow with retro + config fix

- SRE sign-off: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes

- Default thresholds/templates: sources/linear/product-management/PM-618-default-thresholds-and-policy-templates.json
- Observability dashboards: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-913-add-auto-rollback-dashboards-and-alerts.json
- Controller evaluator hook: sources/github/redwood/pr-28411-rollout-controller-hook-slo-evaluator.json
- Rollback executor: sources/github/redwood/pr-28444-rollback-executor-revert-traffic-split-safely.json
- E2E staging tests: sources/github/redwood/pr-28490-e2e-tests-auto-rollback-staging.json

Acceptance criteria
- Written enablement runbook (this ticket) reviewed by SRE + platform leads; posted in release notes thread.
- Flags exist and are documented with defaults per environment.
- Allowlist mechanism supports route/model/region/tier scoping and can be edited without deploy.
- Backout steps verified in staging (flip OFF; confirm no actions executed while eval metrics continue/stop as expected).
- Prod enablement completed through Phase 2 with SRE sign-off and no backout criteria triggered.
comments: 2026-02-21 (Connor O’Brien): Drafted phase plan and flag matrix; aligning with SRE on whether prod default should be EVAL_ONLY for 48h or 72h.

2026-02-24 (Rafael Mendes): Please add explicit criterion for “monitor missing/stale” rate and clarify fail-open vs fail-closed. SRE preference: fail-open (do not rollback) + notify; only act when data fresh + min-sample met.

2026-02-25 (Aisha Bello): For alert routing, start with notify-only to #eng-sre + #eng-platform. Paging should be a separate ticket after we observe baseline volume. Also ensure alert labels include rollout_id and service/route so triage is fast.

2026-02-26 (Jada Williams): Confirmed controller can run in EVAL_ONLY without touching rollout state. For PAUSE_ONLY and above, we must include the PR-28502 lock fix in the release train to avoid double-execution edge case.

2026-02-27 (Leila Farouk): Staging E2E plan ready; we’ll need a stable way to inject synthetic latency into one route without impacting other tests. Suggest gating the injector behind a separate staging-only flag.
2026-02-28 (Sean Gallagher): Looks good. Add explicit call-out that Dedicated/Private remain opt-in and require service owner acknowledgement + runbook link before adding to allowlist.
